doc.title: Lou Donaldson — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Touring with Benson and Lonnie Smith
summary: The group stretched out live and Smith became a long recording partner.

story.theme_name: Leading a band: choosing, paying and managing players
story.community_name: Leading a band: running, choosing and keeping players

blocks.x: You were touring with them in ‘67, ‘68, ‘69...
What was band like live? Were you following the same format or stretching out more?
We stretched out a little more on the “Impressions”(?—53:36) stuff.
Now, your relationship with Lonnie Smith has been ongoing ever since...
...and it’s one of the great partnerships in this music. Can you talk about your interplay?
We were so compatible, we just made records for years—15-20 years.

All of them were selling. That’s another thing. A lot of people say, “Well, you made all those records.” I say, “Yeah, but you got to understand; if you make a record for a company and it doesn’t sell, that’s your last record.” What we did, we’re going to sell some records, even if it’s not a hit. It’s going to sell some records, enough to keep us on the label. It worked that way.
